claim_verdicts.evidence: Round 2: section 3 now uses the round-1 suggested_text. Production environment: "Managed control plane: Let the provider manage the scale and availability of the cluster's control plane, as well as handle patches and upgrades." The address/credentials and "typically has no control-plane node" parts are hedged and follow from the provider running the control plane.

Round 2: section 4 now reads "it keeps it available and handles its patches and upgrades", matching "manage the scale and availability of the cluster's control plane, as well as handle patches and upgrades". The etcd/certificate items are no longer stated as documented facts in prose; they remain in the section 6 table (see minor issue on "That covers the work of the last module").

Round 2: sections 3, 4, 6 and summary line 3 now say a broken node "can be replaced". Docs: "Managed worker nodes: Configure pools of nodes to meet your needs, then the provider makes sure those nodes are available and ready to implement upgrades when needed." Cluster Autoscaler docs speak of "pre-configured Node groups".

Round 2: recast in the ledger as kind opinion (course working model). Lesson text is hedged: "Providers publish which parts they run; for a managed cluster the split usually puts what the team applies on the team's side". No pinned doc assigns the split (Grep "shared responsibility" in refs/kubernetes-website: no match), so it cannot be verified, but it is no longer asserted as a documented rule.

Round 2: section 4 uses the round-1 suggested_text, with the provider part hedged ("usually"). kubeadm-upgrade: "Skipping MINOR versions when upgrading is unsupported." Deprecation guide: "The policy/v1beta1 API version of PodDisruptionBudget is no longer served as of v1.25."

Round 2: section 4 uses the round-1 suggested_text. Service controller "interacts with your cloud provider's APIs to set up load balancers ... when you declare a Service resource that requires them"; dynamic provisioning "automatically provisions storage when users create PersistentVolumeClaim objects". "nothing in the cluster backs up" is consistent: no Kubernetes component copies volume contents.

scripts/k8s/kubeadm.sh line 6 `source scripts/lib/network-lessons.sh`; line 8 `node() { ... docker exec donhang-control-plane "$@"; }`; scripts/lib/network-lessons.sh line 6 `show() { echo "\$ $*"; "$@"; }` (prints, then runs on the host). Block lines 19-36 match the file. Read from the submodule working tree; `git show stage-3:` was not permitted in this session.

Round 2: hedged to "whether it finds control-plane Pods on a managed cluster depends on how the provider runs them"; no default asserted. Static Pod docs: the kubelet creates a mirror Pod on the API server for each static Pod it runs, so a tier=control-plane query only finds Pods if the control plane runs as static Pods on nodes registered with this API server, which the pinned docs leave to the operator.

Unchanged from round 1. docs/team/self-run-components.md lines 28-31 match the block; section 5 now adds "The two controllers here are ones the team installed, not the controllers inside the control plane", which matches the file's "trong cluster là Argo CD, Git server, bộ điều khiển giải mã secret, bộ điều khiển nhận traffic".

Unchanged from round 1. outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/kubeadm.txt: four manifests, four control-plane Pods on donhang-control-plane, CERTIFICATE AUTHORITY ca, etcd-ca, front-proxy-ca. kubeadm-certs.md: "Client certificates generated by kubeadm expire after 1 year."

Round 2: table row now "Usually only those the provider exposes". kubeadm: "The kubeadm ClusterConfiguration object exposes a way for users to override the default flags passed to control plane components such as the APIServer, ControllerManager, Scheduler and Etcd" via extraArgs. Managed half is hedged.
Unchanged from round 1. "Volumes that were dynamically provisioned inherit the reclaim policy of their StorageClass, which defaults to Delete."
Unchanged from round 1. "All Kubernetes objects are stored in etcd." Volume data lives in "the associated storage asset in the external infrastructure".
Round 2: section 8 now says "fails on an API version the API server no longer serves", matching the deprecation guide: "The batch/v1beta1 API version of CronJob is no longer served as of v1.25."
Unchanged from round 1. Opinion in section 7 with explicit conditions; no ranking stated as fact.
Unchanged from round 1. Opinion conditional on a setting or version the provider lacks; premise (claim 11) now hedged.

issues.text: New in round 2 (changed text). After the rephrase the sentence says the provider covers "the work of the last module", which the situation lists as including "upgrading one minor version at a time"; the next paragraph says "Upgrades stay on the team's list." Read alone, the first sentence overstates the hand-off.
issues.quote: That covers the work of the last module.
issues.fix: Write: "That covers most of the work of the last module: the etcd majority, etcd's data, the certificates and the upgrade steps themselves."

issues.text: New in round 2 (changed text). Option e explanation drops the hedge the lesson uses (table: "Usually only those the provider exposes"; claim 11 provider-dependent). Key is still correct: e ("any API server setting") is wrong either way.
issues.quote: On a managed cluster the team gets only the control-plane settings the provider offers.
issues.fix: en: "On a managed cluster the team usually gets only the control-plane settings the provider exposes." vi: "Trên cluster managed, đội thường chỉ có những thiết lập control plane mà nhà cung cấp cho phép."

issues.text: Carried from round 1. From cluster-upgrades I know workers are upgraded one at a time with drain and uncordon. Section 4 says node pools are created and kept available by the provider and that upgrades stay on the team's list, but never says who runs the worker-node upgrade steps in a node pool.
issues.quote: Upgrades stay on the team's list.
issues.fix: Add one sentence saying who runs the worker-node upgrade steps in a node pool and what the team still decides.

issues.text: New in round 2 (changed text). Two paragraphs apart I read that the provider's work "covers the work of the last module" (which the situation says includes upgrading) and then "Upgrades stay on the team's list". I had to go to the table in section 6 to learn the split: provider runs the steps, team picks when.
issues.quote: That covers the work of the last module.
issues.fix: After "Upgrades stay on the team's list." add: "The provider runs the upgrade steps; the team decides when, inside the support window."

issues.text: New in round 2 (changed text). The prose says node pools "sit across the line", but this is the first time section 4 mentions a line, and the diagram puts Node pools wholly inside the Provider box. I can work it out from the "picks template and size" arrow, but the words and the picture disagree at first.
issues.quote: Node pools sit across the line.
issues.fix: Write: "Node pools sit in the provider's box, but the team steers them:" and keep the rest of the paragraph.
